nvitk.segmentation.hemisphere¶

Split bilateral label masks into left/right hemispheres.

Two strategies are provided:

  • split_lr_by_cc() — connected-components driven: keeps the n largest CCs in mask and assigns Left/Right from their world-space x centroids. This is what ct-pet-v5 and dixon-v5 use for the deltoid TotalSegmentator label which ships bilaterally without native L/R classes.

  • split_lr_by_midline() — geometric fallback: split on a sagittal plane (specified by voxel x or auto-detected from the affine origin).

Both functions work for images in any voxel orientation: the sign of the affine’s first column determines which voxel-space side maps to anatomical “left” in world coordinates.

Module Contents¶

nvitk.segmentation.hemisphere.split_lr_by_cc(mask: nvitk.types.Image, *, n: int = 2, structure: Any = None) → tuple[nvitk.types.Image, nvitk.types.Image]¶

Split a bilateral binary mask into (left, right) images using connected components.

The top-n CCs (by size) are kept and labeled L/R via their centroids’ world-space x coordinate (computed with mask.affine). The convention used is the radiology/anatomical one: Left means the subject’s left side, which in a right-handed RAS/LAS coordinate system has the lower x world coordinate; in LPS/LPI it has the higher x coordinate. This is derived from the sign of affine[0, 0] so it works with either convention.

Parameters:

  • mask – 3D binary Image. Its Image.affine is required.

  • n – How many components to keep (default 2, i.e. left + right).

  • structure – Connectivity structure passed to ndi.label.

Returns:

Two images: (left, right). If fewer than 2 CCs are found, the missing one is returned as an empty mask.

Return type:

(Image, Image)

nvitk.segmentation.hemisphere.split_lr_by_midline(mask: nvitk.types.Image, *, plane_x: int | None = None) → tuple[nvitk.types.Image, nvitk.types.Image]¶

Split a bilateral mask by a sagittal (YZ) plane at voxel x = plane_x.

When plane_x is None, the plane is chosen so that its world-x matches the volume’s world-x midpoint (i.e. the geometric midline along the image).

Returns (left, right) following the same lower-world-x -> LEFT convention as split_lr_by_cc().
